Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
• 24-year-old woman with 2-day history of constant dull lower-abdominal ache, nausea, and subjective fever; GP advised urgent face-to-face review to rule out pregnancy (incl. ectopic), urinary tract infection, and other pelvic causes.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant dull ache below umbilicus for 2 days, associated nausea (no vomiting) and feeling hot/sweaty.  
• Course: Gradual onset, persistent; worsening discomfort prompted consult.  
• Associated symptoms:
  – Genitourinary: ↑ urinary frequency; no dysuria, urgency, foul smell. Mild pink tinge noticed in urine (likely vaginal spotting).  
  – Gastrointestinal: Constipation 1 week ago, now resolved; normal BM yesterday; no diarrhoea.  
  – Gynaecologic: LMP ~3 weeks ago; expects period soon. Spotting last 2 days. Sexually active with one partner. Contraception: etonogestrel implant. Unsure if pregnant. No vaginal discharge or dyspareunia.  
  – No light-headedness, syncope, or shoulder-tip pain.

• Pertinent negatives: No vomiting, diarrhoea, urinary pain/urgency, foul urine odor, or vaginal discharge.  

• Past medical history: None reported.  
• Allergies: Amoxicillin (stated).  
• Medications: Etonogestrel (Implanon) implant; no regular oral meds.  
• Social / preventive: Non-smoker, lives with boyfriend; brother has type 1 diabetes.

Examination:
• Video consult only – no vitals or physical exam performed.

Impression:
Undifferentiated lower-abdominal pain with systemic symptoms.
Top considerations (from history and DDx):
1. Early pregnancy / ectopic pregnancy – needs exclusion given pelvic pain, spotting, nausea despite implant contraception.
2. Urinary tract infection (cystitis ± early pyelonephritis) – pelvic discomfort, urinary frequency, subjective fever, but lacks dysuria.
3. Pelvic inflammatory disease – lower-abdominal pain, spotting, systemic symptoms; no discharge makes less likely.
Simple constipation less convincing as bowels now regular and systemic features present.

Plan:
• Arrange same-day face-to-face GP appointment for:
  – Urine pregnancy test ± serum β-hCG to rule out pregnancy/ectopic.  
  – Urinalysis & culture to assess for UTI.  
  – Pelvic and abdominal examination; consider cervical swabs for STI/PID if indicated.  
  – Baseline vitals and abdominal exam (incl. rebound/guarding).  
• Provide safety-net advice: if pain worsens, develops syncope, shoulder pain, heavy bleeding, vomiting, or feels more unwell/light-headed, attend ED urgently.  
• Review results promptly and escalate (e.g., ultrasound, surgical or gyne referral) if pregnancy/ectopic or other serious pathology suspected.  
• Symptomatic relief: maintain hydration; simple analgesia (e.g., acetaminophen) if needed; avoid NSAIDs until diagnosis clarified.

Quality checks
● Missing elements: No vitals, physical exam findings, or objective temperature recorded. No documentation of follow-up booking confirmation.  
● Conflicts: DDx ranked UTI highest; transcript clinician leaned more toward constipation and pregnancy exclusion—both retained in impression.  
● Transcript quality: Clear but lacks objective data and timed cut-off abbreviated discussion; otherwise coherent.
